figures.caption: Figure 1: General structural causal model. The edge e → Y (e) means that the conditional rule ηe(Y | Zc) may vary across domains, not that e is a per-sample causal feature. Style is used by LADDER at the domain-summary level to choose source weights, not as a per-sample classifier input.
Table 1: FMoW-WILDS results over five random seeds. Accuracy, worst-region accuracy, average-region accuracy, and ID-to-test accuracy drop are reported in percentage points.
Figure 3: FMoW-WILDS accuracy and worst-region accuracy on the ID validation, OOD validation, and OOD test splits. Error bars denote standard deviations over five random seeds.
Table 2: iWildCam-WILDS results over five random seeds. Test accuracy, macro F1, and filtered average-group accuracy are reported in percentage points.
Figure 6: iWildCam-WILDS test accuracy and filtered averagegroup accuracy. Error bars denote standard deviations over five random seeds.

Figure 2: Synthetic simulation KNN source-selection ablation overK ∈ {1, . . . , 8} and “All”. The main setting uses K = 4, while “All” removes the KNN truncation and reweights all available source classifiers.

Figure 4: Supplementary style-conditioned pooled ablation in the controlled SCM. Stronger pooled predictors close much of the additive PooledJoint gap, especially in extrapolation, but they also have substantially larger variance across repetitions. LADDER remains competitive in extrapolation and gives the strongest interpolation performance among non-oracle methods.
Table 3: FMoW-WILDS results over five random seeds. Accuracy, worst-region accuracy, average-region accuracy, and ID-to-test accuracy drop are reported in percentage points.
Figure 5: FMoW-WILDS accuracy and worst-region accuracy on the ID validation, OOD validation, and OOD test splits.

Figure 7: FMoW-WILDS KNN source-selection ablation over five random seeds. The main setting uses K = 5, while “All” removes the KNN truncation and reweights all retained source domains. The sweep includes K ∈ {1, 2, 3, 5} and shows that local source selection is stable across nearby neighborhood sizes.

Figure 8: Full FMoW-WILDS t-SNE visualization. Panels (a,b) show the causal representation Zc colored by class and domain, respectively; panels (c,d) show the style representation Z (e) s colored by domain and used for source reweighting.

Figure 9: FMoW-WILDS source-geometry diagnostic over all 55 source-domain pairs. The horizontal axis is the LADDER source style distance computed from learned source style distributions. The vertical axes report bidirectional source-classifier transfer loss, classconditional Zc prototype distance, two Zc summary distances, and label-distribution distance.
Table 4: iWildCam-WILDS results over five random seeds. Test accuracy, macro F1, and filtered average-group accuracy are reported in percentage points.
Figure 10: iWildCam-WILDS test accuracy and filtered average-group accuracy.

Table 5: iWildCam-WILDS worst-location diagnostics over five random seeds. Raw worstlocation accuracy takes the minimum over all target locations; filtered worst-location accuracy and zero-location counts use locations with at least 50 samples.

Figure 12: iWildCam-WILDS KNN source-selection ablation over three random seeds. The main setting fixesK = 6, while “All” removes the KNN truncation and reweights all retained source domains. Across K ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}, K = 5 gives the highest test accuracy and macro F1, whereas K = 6 gives the strongest filtered average-group accuracy, matching the robustness-oriented protocol used in the main experiments.
Table 7: Main implementation settings used for the reported runs. KNN ablations in the supplement vary only K while keeping the remaining training protocol fixed.
